headline: Instrument-mounted demonstrations train an appendectomy policy tested in live rabbits
summary: A Sept. 22 preprint reports an end-to-end pipeline that records instrument pose and jaw state from sensors mounted on a surgeon’s ordinary laparoscopic tools, aligns the sensor channels against robot ground truth, and trains a bimanual policy without robot-collected demonstrations. After closed-loop simulator selection among 31 configurations, the authors retrained on 849 demonstrations from four live rabbits and tested on four additional rabbits; the policy completed appendectomy in three of four under shared autonomy with electrosurgery armed. A surgeon chose the surgical phase because the vision-based phase predictor failed under the deployment endoscope. This is a small animal study, not full autonomy or clinical evidence.
